selected_edition.title: Intermediate-area cylinders in the principal quadratic stratum

abstract.visible_complete_rendering: Delecroix asked for the area spectrum of cylinders on large-genus square-tiled surfaces, highlighting the normalized-area window $[g^{-1/2},2g^{-1/2}]$. For the principal holomorphic quadratic stratum, with the number of squares tending to infinity before the genus, we derive a Poisson limit at every intermediate scale $s_g\to0$, $gs_g\to\infty$. The rescaled cylinder areas converge to a Poisson point process of intensity $dx/(2x)$; compact-window counts converge with every fixed joint moment. The highlighted count tends to $\operatorname{Poisson}((\log2)/2)$, and its mean and variance have the same limit. The proof extracts a uniform Gamma/Dirichlet approximation from the published formulas of Delecroix–Liu and Delecroix–Goujard–Zograf–Zorich, then applies classical assembly identities and elementary tail estimates. The weighted permutation model and its unmarked Poisson approximation are prior results. We explicitly credit the earlier microscopic announcements and retain their unresolved normalization discrepancy with the short problem report. AI tools were used extensively; no external human peer review is asserted.
